'''Ratko Varda''' ({{lang-sr-cyr|Ратко Варда}}; born 6 May 1979) is a Serbian-Bosnian former [[basketball]] player who played professionally for 22 years.<ref>{{cite news |author1=Uroš Marjanović |title=RATKO VARDA: Zbog Džordana sam se umalo upiškio! Miličić je bio talentovaniji od Jokića, koji me pravio budalom |url=https://www.espreso.co.rs/sport/kosarka/348337/ratko-varda-zbog-dzordana-sam-se-umalo-upiskio-milicic-je-bio-talentovaniji-od-jokica-koji-me-pravio-budalom |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=Espreso.co.rs |date=2 October 2019 |language=Serbian}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Intervju - Ratko Varda poslije 22 godine karijere... |url=https://www.rtvbn.com/3891918/intervju-ratko-varda-poslije-22-godine-karijere |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[RTV BN]] |date=1 September 2018 |language=Bosnian}}</ref> Standing at {{height|m=2.13}}, he played the [[Center (basketball)|center]] position. He first represented [[Serbia men's national basketball team|FR Yugoslavia/Serbia and Montenegro junior national team]], and later represented [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national basketball team]] internationally.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ratko Varda Profile|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2011.roundID_7524.playerID_21856.teamID_2602.html|website=fibaeurope.com|accessdate=6 October 2017}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Varda came up through [[KK Partizan|Partizan]]'s youth system and made his debut during the 1995–96 season, before making himself eligible for the [[2001 NBA draft]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/draft2001/playerfiles/ratko_varda.html?nav=ArticleList NBA Draft 2001]</ref> He ended up not getting selected but still found himself on the [[Detroit Pistons]] roster to the start of the 2001–02 season.<ref>{{cite news |author1=Drew Sharp |title=Barrier no bother for Dumars |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98028609/barrier-no-bother-for-dumars/ |access-date=20 March 2022 |work=[[Detroit Free Press]] |date=25 July 2001 |pages=1C, 6C}}</ref> Varda ended up spending two seasons in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] on the rosters of the Pistons and the [[Washington Wizards]]. However, he was officially featured in only 1 game. Varda's first and last NBA game was on February 12, 2002, in a 71–99 loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]] where he played for 5 and half minutes and record 5 points and 1 rebound.

In January 2003, he returned to [[Europe]] and signed with [[KK Union Olimpija|Union Olimpija]] until the end of the 2002–03 season.<ref>[http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2003&mm=01&dd=24&nav_id=81922 Ratko Varda u ljubljanskoj Olimpiji] (in Serbian), b92, January 24, 2003.</ref> In the 2003–04 season he played in the [[Greek Basket League]] with [[Apollon Patras B.C.|Apollon Patras]]. In the 2004–05 season, he played with [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] of the [[Turkish Basketball League]].

In the 2006–07 season, he played in the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]], but he could not finish the season due to an [[anterior cruciate ligament]] in his left knee.<ref>[http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=36539 Ratko Varda se pierde lo que resta de temporada] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110525142945/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=36539 |date=2011-05-25 }} (in Spanish), acb, January 10, 2007.</ref>

On October 29, 2007, he signed for the entire season of the Spanish championship with [[Menorca Bàsquet|ViveMenorca]], having recovered from his knee injury.<ref>{{cite news |title=El ViveMenorca ficha a Ratko Varda hasta final de temporada |url=https://as.com/baloncesto/2007/10/29/mas_baloncesto/1193612402_850215.html |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[Diario AS]] |date=29 October 2007 |language=Spanish}}</ref><ref>[http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=43814 Ratko Varda refuerza el ViveMenorca hasta final de temporada] (in Spanish), acb, October 29, 2007.</ref>

On August 21, 2008, he signed a two-year contract with the Lithuanian champions [[BC Žalgiris]] from [[Kaunas]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Zalgiris brings in Ratko Varda|url=http://www.talkbasket.net/1741-zalgiris-brings-in-ratko-varda.html|accessdate=10 March 2015|publisher=talkbasket.com}}</ref> Because of the financial problems of the club, he left Žalgiris in late November.<ref>{{cite web|title=Zalgiris, center Ratko Varda part ways|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/38761/zalgiris-center-ratko-varda-part-ways|publisher=euroleague.net|accessdate=10 March 2015}}</ref> 

On January 26, 2009, he signed with the Russian club [[BC Khimki]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110723191024/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/ulebcup/home/news/i/43087/448 Khimki adds center Ratko Varda] eurocup, January 26, 2009.</ref> On the last day of 2009, Varda signed a one-month contract with [[Asseco Prokom Gdynia]] of Poland.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/64243/180/item Prokom signs Ratko Varda for one month] euroleague, December 31, 2009.</ref> In 2010, Varda extend his contract with Prokom until the end of the 2010–11 season.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/75420/asseco-prokom-keeps-ratko-varda ASSECO PROKOM keeps Ratko Varda] euroleague, September 10, 2010.</ref>

In August 2011, he returned to his former club [[KK Union Olimpija|Union Olimpija]], signing a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Union Olimpija reunites with Varda|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/87175/union-olimpija-reunites-with-varda|publisher=euroleague.net|accessdate=10 March 2015}}</ref> However, he left the team in December because of the club's financial difficulties and signed with [[BC Azovmash]] from [[Mariupol]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/ukraine/32978/ratko-varda-leaves-union-olimpija-and-signs-with-azovmash-mariupol.html Ratko Varda leaves Union Olimpija and signs with Azovmash Mariupol]</ref> He left the team in March by mutual agreement.<ref>[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/ukraine/36043/ratko-varda-and-azovmash-mariupol-part-ways.html Ratko Varda and Azovmash Mariupol part ways]</ref>

On September 29, 2012, he signed a one-month deal with Iranian club [[Mahram Tehran BC|Mahram Tehran]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ratko Varda mesec dana u Iranu| date=29 September 2012 |url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2012&mm=09&dd=29&nav_id=647170|publisher=b92.net|accessdate=10 March 2015|language=sr}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Ratko Varda signs with Mahram|date=29 September 2012 |url=http://www.court-side.com/news/blog/ratko-varda-signs-with-mahram/|publisher=court-side.com|accessdate=10 March 2015}}</ref>

On November 5, 2012, he signed with [[KK Radnički Kragujevac (2009–2014)|Radnički Kragujevac]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Radnički signed Ratko Varda|url=http://www.abaliga.com/a5485/News/Radnicki_signed_Ratko_Varda.html|accessdate=10 March 2015|publisher=abaliga.com|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://archive.today/20150310140838/http://www.abaliga.com/a5485/News/Radnicki_signed_Ratko_Varda.html|archivedate=10 March 2015}}</ref> In January 2013, he got injured and missed the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Radnicki lost Ratko Varda for three months|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/adriatic-league/98781/radnicki-lost-ratko-varda-for-three-months.html|publisher=sportando.com|accessdate=10 March 2015}}</ref>

On July 31, 2013, he signed a one-year deal with [[KK Mega Vizura|Mega Vizura]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Mega Vizura signs Ratko Varda|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/adriatic-league/60625/mega-vizura-signs-ratko-varda.html|publisher=Sportando.net|accessdate=31 July 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Varda pojačao Mega Vizuru| date=31 July 2013 |url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2013&mm=07&dd=31&nav_id=737975|publisher=B92.net|accessdate=31 July 2013|language=sr}}</ref>

In 2012 and 2013, he captained the [[Republika Srpska national basketball team|Republika Srpska team]] in friendlies against Serbia.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.palelive.com/sport-pale/ratko-varda-predvodi-reprezentaciju-republike-srpske|title=Ratko Varda predvodi reprezentaciju Republike Srpske|date=25 December 2012 |language=sr}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://pressrs.ba/sr/sport/kosarka/story/35476/Srpska+bi+se+plasirala+na+Evro+u+Sloveniji.html|title=Srpska bi se plasirala na Evro u Sloveniji|language=sr}}</ref>

On February 2, 2015, he signed with [[Byblos Club|United Byblos Amchit]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=United Byblos Amchit signs Ratko Varda|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/Bosnia/news/393074/United-Byblos-Amchit-signs-Ratko-Varda|publisher=eurobasket.com|accessdate=2 February 2015}}</ref>

On October 1, 2015, Varda signed with [[KK Kožuv]] of the [[Macedonian First League (basketball)|Macedonian First League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Ratko Varda (ex UBA) is a newcomer at Kozuv|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/FYR%20Macedonia/news/423176/Ratko-Varda-%28ex-UBA%29-is-a-newcomer-at-Kozuv|accessdate=2 October 2015|publisher=eurobasket.com}}</ref> On November 4, 2015, he parted ways with Kožuv after appearing in four league games and two [[Balkan International Basketball League|BIBL]] games.<ref>{{cite web|title=Кожув ја раскина соработката со Ратко Варда|url=http://ekipa.mk/kozhuv-ja-raskina-sorabotkata-so-ratko-varda/|publisher=ekipa.mk|accessdate=5 November 2015|language=mk}}</ref> On December 30, 2015, he signed with the Montenegrin club [[KK Sutjeska|Sutjeska]] for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ratko Varda signs with KK Sutjeska|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/montenegro/186465/ratko-varda-signs-with-kk-sutjeska.html|publisher=sportando.com|accessdate=30 December 2015}}</ref> On February 3, 2016, he left Sutjeska and signed with [[Hekmeh BC|Hekmeh]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]] for the rest of the 2016 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Ratko Varda signs with Sagesse|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/189943/ratko-varda-signs-with-sagesse.html|accessdate=February 3, 2016|work=Sportando.com|date=February 3, 2016}}</ref> On November 7, 2016, he re-signed with Hekmeh.<ref>{{cite news|title=Ratko Varda inks with Sagesse Club|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/216705/ratko-varda-inks-with-sagesse-club.html|accessdate=8 November 2016|work=Sportando.com|date=7 November 2016}}</ref>

On March 7, 2017, Varda announced his retirement.<ref>{{cite news|title=PENZIJA Posle 20 klubova, Varda se od košarke oprostio replikom iz kultnog filma!|url=http://sport.blic.rs/kosarka/domaca-kosarka-i-aba/penzija-posle-20-klubova-varda-se-od-kosarke-oprostio-replikom-iz-kultnog-filma/qvr2wx3|accessdate=7 March 2017|work=sport.blic.rs|date=7 March 2017|language=Serbian}}</ref> However, in October 2017, he returned to professional basketball and signed with Serbian club [[KK Dynamic|Dynamic]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Ratko Varda nastavlja karijeru u 38. godini! |url=https://www.alo.rs/sport/kosarka/ratko-varda-nastavlja-karijeru-u-38-godini/125740/vest |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[Alo!]] |date=4 October 2017 |language=Serbian}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://sportklub.rs/Kosarka/Srbija-KLS/a216120-Ratko-Varda-u-Dinamiku.html|title=Iskusni srpski košarkaš Ratko Varda ove sezone će igrati za beogradski Dinamik.|date=4 October 2017 |publisher=sportklub.rs|accessdate=4 October 2017|language=Serbian}}</ref> On December 30, 2017, he parted ways with Dynamic.<ref>{{cite news|title=Dynamic VIP PAY parted ways with four players|url=http://druga.aba-liga.com/news.php?id=39515|accessdate=30 December 2017|work=druga.aba-liga.com|date=30 December 2017}}</ref>

==National team career==
Varda first represented [[Serbia and Montenegro national basketball team]]. He won the bronze medal at the [[1996 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]] in France, and gold medal at the [[1998 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]] in Italy.<ref name=fiba>[https://web.archive.org/web/20101203005202/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/q/Ratko%20VARDA/pid/21856/_/players.html Ratko VARDA (BIH) participated in 7 FIBA / FIBA Zones events]</ref>

He was on the preliminary 17-man squad of coach [[Svetislav Pešić]] for the [[Eurobasket 2001]] in Turkey.<ref>[http://www.arhiva.serbia.gov.rs/news/2001-07/02/24255.html Pesic announces candidates for EURO 2001]</ref><ref>[https://arhiva.srbija-info.gov.rs/vesti/2001-07/02/25818.html Pešićevi aduti za Tursku]</ref> However he did not make the final roster for the Eurobasket. Three years later he was on [[Željko Obradović]] preliminary squad for the [[Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2004 Summer Olympics]] in Athens. However he and [[Dejan Milojević]] were cut on July 20, 2004.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20141006073003/http://www.beobasket.net/page/news/en.html?view=story&id=6935&sectionId=10 ZELJKO OBRADOVIC CUT VARDA AND MILOJEVIC]</ref><ref>[https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2004&mm=07&dd=21&nav_id=146293 Milojević i Varda "otpali"]</ref><ref>[https://www.sportskacentrala.com/2004/07/20/1246/ Varda i Milojević prvi „precrtani“]</ref>

After not getting opportunity to play for Serbian national team, Varda accepted offer to play for the [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national basketball team]].<ref>[https://sportsport.ba/fudbal/varda-se-prikljucio/20437 Varda se priključio]</ref><ref>[https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2009&mm=07&dd=11&nav_id=370829 Ratko Varda na pripremama BiH]</ref> He represented Bosnian national team in [[FIBA EuroBasket 2009 qualification]] and [[FIBA EuroBasket 2011 qualification]].<ref name=fiba/> He left the Bosnian national team in 2011, after conflict with coach [[Sabit Hadžić]].<ref>[https://sportsport.ba/fudbal/hadzic-prica-besmislice/63046 "Hadžić priča besmislice"], sportsport.ba</ref>

==Personal life==
A [[Serbs|Serb]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kurir.rs/ratko-varda-ne-delim-ljude-na-srbe-i-hrvate-clanak-1235261|title=Ratko Varda: Ne delim ljude na Srbe i Hrvate|date=16 June 2023 |language=sr}}</ref> Varda was born in [[Gradiška, Bosnia and Herzegovina|Gradiška]], [[SR Bosnia and Herzegovina]], [[Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia|SFR Yugoslavia]] (now Bosnia and Herzegovina).  His family moved to Serbia during the [[Bosnian War]]. He has a tattoo of [[Saint George and the Dragon]].
